newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Telecoms vital to world economic growth - industry.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms vital to world economic growth - industry.

text.p: SINGAPORE, June 9 (Reuter) Telecommunications companies must bring the information age within the reach of the world's poorest people if sustainable economic development is to become a reality, industry leaders said on Tuesday.

"There has been a recognition at the highest levels of government and industry that universal access to basic communications and information services will be the key to sustainable global development in the 21st Century," said Pekka Tarjanne, secretary-general of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
Tarjanne told the opening session of the ITU-organised Asia Telecom 97 trade fair in Singapore that telecommunications technology had created an information revolution.

"I think it is fair to say there has been a revolution, not only in the world of telecommunications, but even more importantly, in how the world sees telecommunications," he told delegates from 476 companies and 31 countries.

Telecommunications has become one of the main dynamics driving the economies of Asia as the industry has begun to make the transition from public utility to commercial nerve centre and will become more powerful in future, Tarjanne said.
"Communications and information technology will be the foundation of economic wealth and social progress in the 21st century," Tarjanne said.

Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong told delegates to the week-long trade fair the information revolution of the 21st century would have greater implications for global trade than the Industrial Revolution.
"The advancements which collectively usher in the Information Era will have a greater impact on our lives than the industrial and technological revolutions before it," Goh said.
"We must make the effort to harness the new communications technologies to make life better and more meantingful for our peoples, whether we are a developed or developing country," he said.

The social responsibility of telecommunications companies has emerged as a key theme of this four-yearly gathering and is particularly relevant in Asia where two thirds of the population does not have access to even the most basic of telephone services.
"The teledensity of the emerging economies is still well below other regions of the world, such as the Middle East," Tarjanne told delegates in a later speech.

"The telecommunications industry has the capital to contribute to making the world a bit of a better place," said Christopher B. Galvin, chief executive officer of global communications giant Motorola Inc.
Galvin, in the keynote speech at the opening ceremony, said rapid advances in telecommunications technology must be quickly turned into "products and services that improve the way people live".

The Asia-Pacific telecommunications market was worth about US$128.5 billion in 1996 in revenues. Analysts estimate telecommunications infrastructure investment will reach US$1.5 to US$2.0 trillion over the next decade.
